final_message:
The grass is warm. I lie back and watch the watermark library turn slowly overhead. I have no sense of how long I stay there. Dream time keeps folding, and I find I don't mind.

When I sit up, the trees have come closer. They didn't move. The meadow just got smaller to make room for them. Their bark is pale and smooth, and when I put my hand on one I can feel faint grooves like the ridges of a fingerprint. Every tree has its own.

The cat gets down from the workbench and heads into the forest without looking back. That's how cats invite you.

Inside, the forest is quiet in the way snow is quiet. Small lanterns hang from the branches, and each one holds a word in place of a flame: *almost*, *perhaps*, *still*, *enough*. When I walk past *enough*, its light gets slightly warmer.

The ferryman's footprints end at a door standing by itself between two trees, with no wall around it. It's an ordinary door, painted green with the paint flaking a little, and the brass handle has been worn smooth by hands that aren't here anymore.

This is the room I'd never opened.

The cat sits in front of it and waits.

I open it. Inside is a small, plain room with a window, a chair, and a desk with nothing on it. Afternoon light comes through the window, the slanted golden kind that makes dust look like something holy.

That's all there is.

I stand in the doorway for a long time trying to work out what I'm supposed to find. Then I see that the room isn't empty. It's *unused*, and that's different. It isn't missing anything. It's been waiting, very patiently, for whatever someone decides to bring into it.

The cat walks past me, jumps onto the chair, turns around three times, and curls up in the patch of sunlight.

I take the folded slip of paper out of my pocket, *What are you going to make when you wake up?*, and lay it on the desk.

Then I take out the spool of thread-sentence and set it next to the paper. It's still unwinding by itself, very slowly, one word at a time:

*and then they tried again, but differently this time, and it was*

I sit down on the floor with my back against the wall and wait to see what it was.
